questions.title: Ask the Right Questions to Find the Best Boat Insurance for You
questions.body:
Questions to consider for yourself

  • How do I use my boat? Where do I dock or store it? Think about your boating habits—weekend cruises, fishing trips, or long voyages—and where you keep your boat (marina, trailer, or driveway). This helps determine the coverage level you need.
  • Who else will be operating my boat? Will family, friends, or renters use it? Their experience and frequency of use can affect your insurance needs.
  • Do I need any additional coverage like towing or salvage? Consider extras like on-water towing, fuel spill liability, or salvage costs for your boat’s specific risks.

Questions to ask your agent

  • Do I qualify for any savings or discounts? Ask about discounts for safe boating courses, bundling with home insurance, or secure storage (e.g., a locked marina).

  • Are there coverage requirements for boating in Florida? While Florida doesn’t mandate boat insurance, some marinas or lenders do—confirm what’s required for your situation.

  • What isn’t covered by my boat insurance policy? Understand exclusions like wear and tear, marine life damage, or uninsured boater incidents to avoid surprises.

questions.title: What is condo insurance?
questions.body: Condo insurance, also known as HO-6 insurance, is a policy designed to protect condo owners. It provides coverage for the interior of your unit, your personal belongings, and liability risks. Unlike homeowners insurance, it complements the condo association’s master policy, which typically covers the exterior and communal areas. Condo insurance helps ensure your individual unit and possessions are protected from unexpected events.

questions.title: What doesn’t condo insurance cover?
questions.body:
While condo insurance offers valuable protection, it does not cover everything. Exclusions typically include:

  • Flood Damage: Like homeowners insurance, flood damage isn’t included and requires a separate flood insurance policy.
  • Master Policy Coverage: Damage to the exterior of the building and shared spaces is usually covered by the condo association’s master policy.
  • Wear and Tear: Routine maintenance and gradual wear are not covered.
  • Earthquake Damage: (in Florida?)
  • High-Value Items: Items like expensive jewelry or rare collectibles may need additional coverage through endorsements or riders.

questions.title: What are the right questions to ask to find the best condo insurance?
questions.body:
When searching for the right condo insurance in Florida, asking the right questions can help you make an informed decision. Consider these questions:

  • What does my condo association’s master policy cover, and where does my responsibility begin?
  • What risks, like hurricanes or wind damage, are explicitly covered or excluded in my policy?
  • Does the policy include coverage for assessments by the condo association?
  • Do I need flood insurance for my condo?
  • How much coverage do I need for my personal belongings and interior upgrades?
  • What is the deductible for hurricane or wind-related damage?
  • Are there any discounts available, such as for security systems or updated building codes?

questions.title: What is Flood Insurance?
questions.body: Flood insurance is a type of policy that protects homeowners, renters, and businesses from financial losses caused by flooding. It covers damages resulting from overflowing rivers, heavy rainfall, storm surges, and other natural flood events. Standard homeowners insurance policies typically do not cover flood-related damages, making standalone flood insurance essential for those living in flood-prone areas, especially in Florida.

questions.title: What Doesn’t Flood Insurance Cover?
questions.body:
• Groundwater or Sewer Backups: Damage caused by sewer backups or groundwater seepage unless it resulted directly from a flood event and is covered by the policy.
  • Additional Living Expenses: Temporary housing or living expense costs while your home is under repair (most flood policies don’t include this unless added).
  • Exterior Property: Landscaping, swimming pools, decks, patios, and fences are typically not covered.
  • Vehicles: Damage to cars and other vehicles due to flooding is not covered by flood insurance—it’s usually included in comprehensive auto insurance policies.
  • Small Damages Below the Deductible: Any damage less than your policy’s deductible amount.

questions.title: Ask the right questions to find the best auto insurance for you
questions.body:
To choose the most suitable flood insurance for your needs, consider asking the following questions:

  • Am I located in a high-risk flood zone?
  • How much coverage do I need for my home’s structure and personal belongings?
  • What is the deductible, and how does it affect my premium?
  • Does the policy include any exclusions that I should be aware of?
  • Can I add coverage for additional living expenses or other extras?
  • Is coverage available through the National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP), or should I consider private insurers?
  • What is the waiting period for the policy to go into effect?
  • Are there discounts for bundling my flood insurance with other policies?
  • How does this policy address specific flood risks during hurricane season?

By working with a knowledgeable agency like Culbertson Agency, you can ensure your plan is customized to meet your needs and keep your property protected, even during Florida’s unpredictable hurricane season.

questions.title: What is Florida homeowners insurance?
questions.body: Florida Homeowners Insurance is a type of policy designed to protect your home and personal belongings against unexpected events. It provides coverage for damage caused by specific hazards, as well as liability protection if someone is injured on your property. This kind of insurance gives you peace of mind, knowing that your investment and personal assets are safeguarded.

questions.title: What doesn’t homeowners insurance cover?
questions.body:
While homeowners insurance offers broad protection, it does not cover everything. Common exclusions include:

  • Flood Damage: Standard policies do not cover flooding; a separate flood insurance policy is needed, especially in Florida’s high-risk areas.
  • Earthquake Damage …but something tells us you’re not worried about that!
  • Wear and Tear or gradual maintenance issues, like roof aging, which are considered the homeowner’s responsibility.
  • High-Value Items: Items like fine jewelry or art may require additional endorsements or riders for complete coverage.

questions.title: What are the right questions to ask to find the best homeowners insurance?
questions.body:
Finding the right homeowners insurance policy can feel overwhelming. Start by asking these important questions to ensure you’re getting the protection you need:

  • What perils or disasters are covered and excluded in my policy? (Pay special attention to hurricane and flood risks in Florida.)

  • How much coverage do I need for my home’s structure?

  • What is the deductible for hurricane or wind damage? (Florida policies often include separate deductibles for hurricanes.)

  • Is my personal property fully covered, or do I need additional coverage for specific items?

  • What discounts or savings options are available?

  • Does my policy include liability protection, and at what limits?

  • Are there any additional coverage options I should consider for Florida-specific risks?

questions.title: What is life insurance?
questions.body: Florida Life Insurance is a contract between you and an insurance provider that offers financial protection to your loved ones after you pass away. By paying regular premiums, you ensure that your beneficiaries receive a death benefit, which can help cover expenses like funeral costs, debts, or ongoing living expenses. Some types of life insurance may also include savings or investment components that you can access during your lifetime.

questions.title: What doesn’t life insurance cover?
questions.body:
While life insurance offers valuable protection, it does have some exclusions. Common exclusions include:

  • Fraudulent Information: If false information was provided on your application.
  • Death by Suicide: Death caused by suicide may not be covered within the first two years of the policy (this varies by provider).
  • Risky Activities: Deaths from high-risk activities like skydiving or car racing may not be covered unless explicitly added to the policy.
  • Illegal Activities: Death resulting from illegal acts may void the policy.
  • Non-Payment of Premiums: If premiums are not paid, the policy may lapse and result in no coverage.

questions.title: What are the right questions to ask to find the best life insurance?
questions.body:
Finding the right life insurance for your needs is crucial. Here are key questions to ask when choosing a policy:

  • What type of life insurance—term or whole life—is best for my situation?
  • How much coverage do I need to protect my family’s financial future?
  • What is the length of the policy term, and can it be renewed or converted later?
  • Are there any exclusions or specific conditions I should be aware of?
  • Does the policy have any additional features, like living benefits or riders?
  • What are the premium costs, and will they change over time?
  • Can I customize the policy to meet my family’s specific needs and goals?
  • Does the insurer have a strong reputation and financial stability?

By working with an experienced agency like Culbertson Agency, you can explore your options and select a life insurance plan that fits your needs and provides peace of mind for your family’s future.

questions.title: What is renters insurance?
questions.body: Renters insurance is a policy designed to protect people who rent their homes or apartments. It covers your personal belongings, liability, and additional living expenses if your rental becomes unlivable due to a covered event. While your landlord’s insurance covers the building itself, renters insurance ensures your possessions and personal liability are protected.

questions.title: What doesn’t renters insurance cover?
questions.body:
• Flood Damage: Most policies don’t include flood coverage; a separate policy is required.
  • Hurricane Storm Surge Damage** – Water damage caused by storm surge might also need additional coverage.
  • Roommate Belongings: Unless specifically listed, your roommate’s items aren’t covered under your policy.
  • Pest Infestation: Damage caused by bed bugs, termites, or rodents isn’t included.
  • Negligence: Damages you cause due to intentional or careless actions typically aren’t covered.
  • Vehicles and Motorized Equipment: Cars, boats, or motorized equipment you own aren’t included; separate insurance is needed.

questions.title: What are the right questions to ask to find the best renters insurance?
questions.body:
• What disasters are covered under this policy?
  • Does the policy cover damages from hurricanes or windstorm-related incidents?
  • Is flood insurance recommended or necessary based on where I live?
  • What’s the limit and deductible for personal belongings coverage?
  • Are high-value items like jewelry or electronics fully covered?
  • Can I bundle renters insurance with other policies for a discount?
  • Does liability coverage include injuries caused by my pets?
  • What’s the process and timeline for filing claims?
  • Are there any exclusions I should know about for the area of Florida I live in?
  • Does the policy cover additional living expenses during hurricane evacuations?
